title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_---1LD_1LA0LF_0LB0LC_1RB0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_---1LD_1LA0LF_0LB0LC_1RB0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of pairs of numbers written as 1^a 0 (01)^b; the sweep rules over the pieces are proved in Lean, but the evolution of the list has no known rule. No halt in 1010 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: E with 0 two left, 0 left, 0 under the head; F with 0 two left, 0 left, 1 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: 6 rules for all values of the repeat counts and every tape around them: the rightward sweep turning 01 into 10 (A) and back (B), the leftward sweep turning (01)^n and (10)^n into blocks of ones (C, D) or (01)^n, and the turn at the right end.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 29,678 cells have been visited and 24,425 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_---1LD_1LA0LF_0LB0LC_1RB0LB 10000000000 runs 1010 steps without a halt (72,994 ones at the end).

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).

claims.title: Pairs 1^a 0 (01)^b
claims.text: At every 31st visit to the right end in the first 3·108 steps, 98.7% of the tape is covered by pieces 1^a 0 (01)^b with a at least 2. The difference a − b is usually 1 (8,496 pieces), −1 (4,122), 2 or 3, but ranges from −13 to 25.

claims.title: The halting state is never close
claims.text: C0 is the only halting transition and C is entered only by B0 (1LC). When B comes from A0 or F0 (both 1RB) the cell C reads is the 1 just written, so a halt needs B to come from E0 or F1 (0LB) onto two 0s: 0 0 E>0 or 0 0 F>1. In the first 109 steps C is entered 157,760,038 times and reads 1 every time.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 24 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The pieces are crossed by proved rules, but how a round trip rewrites the list of pairs (a, b) is not understood; a proof needs an invariant of the list that keeps two 0s away from where E or F turn left.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a list of pairs of numbers, each written as a block of ones followed by a stretch of 01s; every round trip the two numbers of a pair change roles and the list is rewritten. This page shows the encoding, the proved rules and what a halt would need.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
The sweep rules of lean/Rules.lean, for every repeat count.

sections.heading: A list of pairs (a, b)
sections.html: The head sweeps from end to end; a visit adds 3 or 5 cells at each end. After a rightward sweep the tape is a sequence of pieces 1^a 0 (01)^b: a block of a ones, a 0, and b copies of 01 (98.7% of the tape is covered this way). The leftward sweep turns each stretch (01)^b into a block of 2b ones (C, rule left_C) and blocks of ones into stretches of 01 or 10: the two numbers of a pair trade their encodings every round trip. The rightward sweep shifts the 01 stretches by one cell (A and B). In most pieces a − b is 1 or −1, but it ranges from −13 to 25; the list as a whole evolves like a cellular automaton with no known rule.

sections.heading: The sweep rules
sections.html:
Each row is a theorem of lean/Rules.lean, for every n and every tape L, R (S>: the head in state S on the next cell; (w)^n: n copies of w; 0^inf: blank tape).

rulefromtostepswhat it says
right_AL A> (01)^n RL (10)^n A> R2 · nRightward sweep: A turns 01 into 10.
right_BL B> (10)^n RL (01)^n B> R2 · nRightward sweep: B turns 10 into 01.
left_CL (01)^n C> 1 RL C> 1 (11)^n R4 · nLeftward sweep: C turns each 01 into 11: a stretch (01)^n becomes a block of 2n ones.
left_DL (10)^n D> 1 RL D> 1 (11)^n R4 · nLeftward sweep: D turns each 10 into 11.
left_C2L (10)^n C> 1 RL C> 1 (01)^n R4 · nLeftward sweep: C turns 10 into 01.
right_endL 0 A> 0^infL D> 0 1 1 0^inf3Right end, arrival in A: new cells, and D turns back.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
sections.html: C0 is the only halting transition and C is entered only from B on a 0 (writing 1, moving left). B is entered from A0 and F0, both writing a 1 and moving right, so C then reads that 1; and from E0 and F1, both writing 0 and moving left. So a halt needs 0 0 E>0 or 0 0 F>1: E or F turning left onto two 0s. At the right end the head always arrives in A or B after a 1, which is safe. In the first 109 steps C is entered 157,760,038 times and reads 1 every time; no halt in 1010 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).
After 109 steps the tape spans 29,678 cells (10,642 left of the start, 11,115 right), with a density of 1s of 0.823.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer whose tape, after a rightward sweep, is a sequence of pairs 1^a 0 (01)^b; the leftward sweep turns each (01)^b into a block of 2b ones, so the two numbers of a pair trade places every round trip, and the list evolves like a cellular automaton; halting needs B to land on two 0s from the right, never seen.
family: bouncer over a list of number pairs
